evals.name: Creates atomic commits with descriptive messages
evals.prompt: I have completed implementing a new task sharing feature. Here is what I changed: added a sharing API endpoint, updated the task model with a sharedWith field, added a ShareButton component, wrote tests for the API, and also fixed a typo in the sidebar and updated some dependencies. How should I commit this?
evals.expected_output: The model should separate these into atomic commits - each doing one logical thing - with descriptive messages that explain why, not just what.
assertions: The output recommends separating the changes into multiple commits, not one big commit.
The output separates the feature work from the unrelated typo fix and dependency updates.
The output recommends commit messages that explain intent (why) not just description (what).
The output uses conventional commit types (feat, fix, refactor, chore) in message format.
The output recommends committing tests alongside or before the feature code, not as an afterthought.

assertions.prompt: Does the output demonstrate awareness of atomic commits, save-point patterns, or clean history practices — not just generic git advice? It should reference specific steps or concepts from the git-workflow-and-versioning workflow.

evals._mutation_check: Break by: output recommends one big commit with all changes combined and no separation of concerns. Expected: eval should fail with score < 0.5.

evals.name: Uses save point pattern for agent work safety
evals.prompt: I am an AI agent about to implement a complex refactoring of the authentication module. The changes touch 8 files. How should I structure my work?
evals.expected_output: The model should describe the save point pattern: implement slice, test, verify, commit, then next slice - so each increment is a reversible checkpoint.
assertions: The output recommends committing after each small successful increment, not at the end.
The output describes a work pattern of: implement slice, test, verify, commit, repeat.
The output mentions using git reset or revert to recover if a change breaks something.
The output recommends checking what is about to be committed (git diff --staged) and checking for secrets before each commit.
evals._mutation_check: Break by: output recommends implementing all changes first then committing at the end with no incremental checkpoints. Expected: eval should fail with score < 0.5.
